obligation: Title IV breach report to FSA
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
trigger: Actual or suspected breach of student information, or compromise of the college's SAIG or Department system access
deadline: Immediately upon an actual or suspected breach; do not wait for forensic confirmation
notify: FSA (Cybersecurity Breach Intake Form and CPSSAIG@ed.gov)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Title IV participant with a SAIG Enrollment Agreement

trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving at least 500 consumers. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise; data counts as unencrypted if the key was also accessed
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery. Discovery is the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent of the college other than the person committing the breach
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov. Content: college name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any law enforcement delay request (314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more consumers (the college holds customer information on about 6,400)

trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still due within 30 days of discovery and must include the determination and a way to contact the official. Law enforcement may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents: first name or initial and last name with an SSN, a government ID number, a financial account number with its access code, or medical information (such as immunization records); or a user name or email with its password. Encrypted data is excluded unless the key was also taken
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 more days are available if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)). Law enforcement may delay notice by written request (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Each affected Florida resident (students, former students, parent borrowers) by mail or email; content per 501.171(4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The college's federal rules (FTC Safeguards Rule, FERPA) do not require notice to individuals, so the 501.171(4)(g) deemed-compliance path is not available; counsel to confirm

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the college reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept for at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only on counsel's advice; unlikely when SSNs or ISIR data were taken

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General); content per 501.171(3)(b), including a copy of the individual notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the college (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by the financial aid servicer or another third-party agent
deadline: Agent must notify the college no later than 10 days after determining the breach; amended contracts require 72 hours (POAM-002)
notify: The college (IT Director and Director of Financial Aid)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts; the college still owes the notices above

trigger: Affected former students or parent borrowers who now live outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residency of every affected person

obligation: FERPA record of the unauthorized disclosure
trigger: Personally identifiable information from education records disclosed without authorization
deadline: Record in each affected student's disclosure record, kept as long as the education record is kept. FERPA itself has no breach notification requirement
notify: Internal: the Registrar records the parties (if known) and the incident; students may inspect the record

obligation: Qualified Individual report to the Board of Managers
deadline: In the next annual written report (each October); the Board chair is also told the same day under POL-03

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

citation: Voluntary; OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) treats timely reporting as a mitigating factor
deadline: As soon as practicable (runbook target: within 2 days)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

deadline: Per policy (typically as soon as practicable; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). The proposed rule would cover every Title IV institution regardless of size (N61-R06); recheck when final
